clue.text: Enormous deficit in fuel

indicators.note: in tells us the word for deficit sits inside the word for fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge shortfall in the fuel supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of gigantic size; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Stop losing energy, for instance

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the word for stop

parts.note: to cease is to stop
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Stop wasting energy, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A case in point is an example, so case means an instance.

clue.text: Plunder, large amount to carry over

indicators.note: to carry means to hold inside, so the large amount holds the letter for over

parts.note: a lot is a large amount
O stands for over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Stolen goods, a big haul to be carried across.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is stolen goods or booty taken by force.

clue.text: Thus a religious leader starts to rage about continuing drama

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A pontiff beginning to fume over an ongoing drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial broadcast that runs on indefinitely, so it is a continuing drama.

clue.text: Town in Australia is place not usually supported by bands

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supported by another sits above it
not usually suggests the letters of is place are not in their usual order

parts.note: rings are bands, as on a finger

explanation.surface: An Australian outback town whose location is unusually held up by bands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not usually' rearranges IS PLACE into ALICESP, which stands above RINGS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in the Northern Territory of Australia.

clue.text: Make up for bad part of tennis match

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
a tennis match is divided into sets

explanation.surface: Compensating for a poor stretch of a tennis game.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset a loss is to counterbalance or compensate for it.

clue.text: Wind instrument following stringed instrument

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, used in page references
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A woodwind piece follows a stringed one in the concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A flute is a woodwind instrument played by blowing across a hole.

clue.text: Ground is natural area for festival

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters are crushed and reformed

explanation.surface: A natural patch of ground is the venue for a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun, but it means milled and signals rearranging IS NATURAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was an ancient Roman winter feast in honour of Saturn.

clue.text: A passionate speech in order, followed by a lively dance

indicators.note: in puts the first two pieces inside the word for order

parts.note: to tell someone to do something is to order them
a rant is an impassioned tirade

explanation.surface: An angry speech, delivered in order, then a jolly dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance.

clue.text: Police in retreat, admitting botched raid, scattered

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so the anagram goes inside the other piece
a retreating force goes backwards, so the word for police is read from the end

parts.note: cops are police officers

indicators.note: a botched job is messed up, so the letters of raid are jumbled

explanation.surface: Police pulling back after a bungled raid, scattering in all directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reads like the police pulling back, but it signals reading their name backwards; 'botched' scrambles the raid, and 'admitting' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic events are occasional and dispersed, as are scattered ones.

clue.text: Club membership finally complete

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word membership

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: Full club membership achieved at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is a golf club used on the green, so club names the category.

clue.text: Emotionless, almost give up in dull court

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the dull and court pieces

parts.note: a matte finish is dull, not glossy

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from bottom to top
almost means the word for give loses its last letter

parts.note: to afford is to give or provide

explanation.surface: An unfeeling person nearly surrenders in a dreary courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'give up' looks like a phrase meaning surrender; in fact 'give' is AFFORD, 'almost' cuts it to AFFOR, and 'up' turns that to ROFFA, which goes 'in' MATTE + CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter-of-fact manner is plain and unsentimental, showing no feeling.

clue.text: Solid teacher occupied by poem about unruly herd

indicators.note: a place occupied by people has them inside it, so the other pieces go within the teacher word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
an ode is a lyric poem
ca is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: unruly suggests disorder, so the letters of herd are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher reciting a poem about an unruly herd of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' is the geometric noun, not an adjective; 'unruly' scrambles the herd before everything goes inside the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-faced polyhedron is a three-dimensional geometric solid.

clue.text: Leave sailor in small club in charge, with endless beer

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the small and club pieces

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sport
AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: endless means the beer word loses its final letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A sailor in a small club, in charge, with an endless supply of beer, takes time off.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabbatical is a period of paid leave from work, often for study or travel.

clue.text: Characteristic conclusion of Iago, sour, terribly disloyal

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

indicators.note: conclusion of picks out the last letter of Iago
terribly suggests the letters of sour are badly mixed up

explanation.surface: Iago's sour end is typical of the treacherous villain of Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges SOUR into ROUS. Iago is the treacherous schemer in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Traitorous behaviour betrays trust, which is what being disloyal means.

clue.text: Engineers in time share opinion

indicators.note: in places the engineers inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: Engineers eventually coming round to the same view.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to hold the same view as someone else.

clue.text: Revolutionary work by number two initially bothered ruler

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so the short word for work is turned backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
ten is a number

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word two

parts.note: something eating you bothers you, so ate means bothered

explanation.surface: A deputy, troubled by a revolutionary work, falls out with the leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number two' looks like a deputy, but splits into a number and the first letter of two; 'Revolutionary' turns the work round.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or autocrat with great power.

clue.text: Iguana running wild around vehicle in country

indicators.note: around means the anagram wraps round the vehicle word
running wild suggests the letters of iguana are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A lizard running amok around a car in a Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running wild' scrambles the lizard's name, which then goes 'around' the vehicle; the animal is fodder, not part of the scene's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaragua is a nation in Central America.

clue.text: Officer right at stern of ship shortened farewell

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the letter for right comes at the end

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: shortened means the farewell word loses its final letter

parts.note: adieu is French for goodbye

explanation.surface: An officer standing at the back of a ship offers a clipped goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army rank, commanding a brigade.

clue.text: Not well after church? Relax

indicators.note: after puts the word for unwell behind the church abbreviation

parts.note: ill means not well

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell after the church service, someone is told to take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill, in slang, is to unwind or calm down.

clue.text: Article about old rugged remote road

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the article goes round the other pieces

parts.note: the is the definite article
rugged terrain is rough
remote means far away

explanation.surface: An article about an old rough and remote track.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public street.

clue.text: Colour in loch reflected

indicators.note: in tells us the colour is concealed within the phrase loch reflected

explanation.surface: A colour mirrored in the waters of a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' tempts a reversal, but the colour runs forwards across the two words. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment and shade.

clue.text: Formerly working around east

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
C is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: In the past, someone was working around the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, previously.

clue.text: Theatrical work quietly put down

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to lay is to put something down

explanation.surface: A stage drama is quietly set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a drama written to be staged in a theatre.

clue.text: Cover for plant, see, not finished by man

indicators.note: by means next to, so the word for man is placed alongside
not finished means the slang word for see loses its last letter

parts.note: to clock something is slang for to notice or see it
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man left a plant cover unfinished, by the look of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts CLOCK to CLOC. A cloche is a bell-shaped glass or plastic cover for young plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloche is a bell-shaped protective dome put over garden seedlings.

clue.text: Alarming changes for unsafe seat?

indicators.note: changes signals rearranging the letters of alarming

explanation.surface: Worrying swings of opinion threaten a political seat.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK politics a marginal is a constituency won by a narrow majority, which could easily change hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal constituency is held by a slim majority, so it is at risk at an election.

clue.text: Lower class by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word is spoken and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a lesson is a class at school

explanation.surface: A lower class, judging by how it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to reduce or diminish, so to lower a level.

clue.text: Plan from renegade for example in filthy place

indicators.note: in places the turncoat and example abbreviation inside the dirty place

parts.note: a sty, or pigsty, is a filthy place
a rat is a deserter or traitor

explanation.surface: A turncoat's scheme, hatched in a squalid hovel.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall scheme for achieving a goal.
